transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. It’s lovely to meet you, too. 

I, um... well, I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing. I'm a secondary school teacher, and lately I've just been having a bit of a hard time shaking off some... thoughts, I guess? 

It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, and I know it probably sounds strange, but I keep getting this feeling that certain staff emails, or even the morning announcements over the PA system, are actually... well, coded messages meant specifically for me. 

Some of the other teachers—who are just wonderful, by the way—they've gently shown me that those emails are just standard memos sent to everyone on staff. And I know they are! I really do. But I just can't quite seem to shake the feeling that they're about me anyway. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up today? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way for you.
When you have these thoughts, do you believe the emails and announcements really are coded messages for you?

Oh, well... I mean, intellectually, I know they aren't. I don't want to sound completely unreasonable! When my colleagues show me their computer screens and I can see the exact same memo went out to the whole staff, I completely agree with them. I see it right there in black and white. 

But... um... it's just that, I suppose, deep down, I still kind of believe it anyway? 

It's so embarrassing to admit, but even with them gently showing me the emails were sent to everyone, I just can't seem to shake the feeling that the real message is still somehow directed at me. Like there's a second layer to it that only I'm supposed to understand. I try so hard to just ignore it and go about my lesson planning, I promise I do. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too foolish... I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly.
Do you ever think, even briefly, that these messages might just be a misinterpretation by your own mind?

Oh, absolutely. I tell myself that all the time! I really do. I sit at my desk and I think, 'You're just misinterpreting things, it's just your mind working overtime.' And I want to believe that so badly... because it would make me so much less of a bother to everyone. 

But... um... and I feel so silly admitting this to you... no matter how hard I try to rationalize it, I just can't shake the feeling that those staff emails and morning announcements really are coded messages about me. Even when my colleagues are so sweet and gently show me that they were sent to absolutely everyone on staff... that feeling just sticks right there in my chest and I can't let it go. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably makes me sound terribly stubborn, or like I'm refusing to listen to reason. I promise I really am trying my best to be logical about it. Is... is that a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Oh... um... well. I suppose... and I really hope this doesn't make me sound completely unhinged, doctor... but, yes. Sometimes. 

It's only ever when it's very quiet. Like when I'm at home by myself, or after all the students have left my classroom for the day and I'm just tidying up. I'll hear... well, a woman's voice. Usually she's just saying my name, or maybe making a very short little comment about whatever I happen to be doing at that moment. 

It's so brief, really! But it sounds clear enough that a few times I've actually answered back out loud, just out of habit, before I look up and realize the room is completely empty. 

I always tell myself it's just stress, or my ears playing tricks on me when I'm tired. I really hope that doesn't sound too alarming... I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right picture. Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
Have you had a period where your mood felt unusually high, excited, or full of energy?

Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. I mean, I certainly get happy when my students do well on their exams, or when a lesson plan goes perfectly! But... not unusually high or bursting with energy. 

To be perfectly honest, teaching teenagers all day usually leaves me feeling quite the opposite. I'm mostly just a bit worn out by the time I get home. 

I hope it's alright to say no to that one? I haven't really experienced anything like what you're describing, but I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer. Did I understand your question correctly?
About how long have you been having these experiences?

Oh, um... let me think. It really hasn't been terribly long, I promise. I'd say... well, the worries about the coded messages, and... and that little voice I sometimes answer... it's been about four months. Yes, right around four months. 

I really thought it was just a temporary thing, you know? Just a little phase from being overtired at school that would pass on its own. I hope waiting four months to talk about it doesn't make it sound like I've been hiding things from anyone... I just kept hoping it would fade away so I wouldn't have to bother anyone or make a fuss about it. 

Does that timeline help you? I can try to look back at my calendar and pinpoint an exact week if you need me to, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
During this time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I have my days, of course, just like anyone else. Sometimes grading papers all weekend can make me feel a little bit down or overwhelmed, but... definitely not every day, and certainly not most of the day. 

I actually try very hard to stay positive, especially for the students. They really need a cheerful environment, you know? So I make sure to keep a smile on my face and push through any little slumps. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around being gloomy all the time. I'm really trying my best to stay upbeat through all of this... is that the right way to handle it, doctor?
Have these experiences made it harder for you to do your job or manage your day-to-day life?

Oh... well... I suppose it has, just a little bit. But I'm still teaching! I haven't missed any days of school, I promise. I've just... well, I've had to ask a few of the other teachers to help cover parts of my project lessons, just lately. And they've been so kind to help me get through our planning meetings when I get a little distracted. 

I feel terrible asking them for help, I really do. I don't want to be a burden on anyone at work. And outside of school... well, I haven't been quite as reliable for my book club, or the community theater, or our neighborhood events. I've just been staying home a bit more. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incompetent, doctor. I'm really trying very hard to keep everything together and not let anyone down. Is it... is it normal to need a little extra help like that right now?
Have you been taking care of yourself as usual—for example with bathing, dressing, and keeping up your home?

Oh, yes, absolutely! I've been taking care of myself. I make sure to shower and dress nicely every morning for school, of course. I'd never want to look unkempt in front of the students or the other teachers. 

My home is... well, it's mostly fine. I might be a tiny bit behind on a few chores, just little things like dusting or folding the laundry right away. I've been a little tired, so sometimes the dishes sit in the sink for an extra day. But it's certainly not a disaster zone or anything like that! I promise I'm keeping things tidy enough. 

I hope it's okay that I'm not keeping a perfectly spotless house right now. I'm trying to prioritize my energy for work, you know? Do you think that's the right balance to strike?
When these problems first began, did the strange beliefs and the voice come on very suddenly—within about two weeks?

Oh... um, no, it wasn't like that at all. It wasn't sudden. It... well, it kind of just crept up on me, very slowly. I'd say it took a few months, really, before I even realized things were... different. 

I think that's better, right? That it didn't just happen all at once? I mean, I was still functioning perfectly fine while it was starting. I didn't just wake up one morning and... and lose my grip on things. It was very gradual. I hope that means it's not as serious, doctor?
